text:
Adrian Kempe is doing a lot of things right for the Kings and getting very little back for it. The Kings have 59% of the expected goals (the quality of the chances) at five on five with him on the ice, nearly 13 points better than without him, one of the best marks on the team. But he has six goals on 8.6 expected, and Los Angeles has scored 5.5 fewer goals than expected with him out there. That's the Kings' season in one player.

He's 30, a Kings lifer with 729 games for the club, and one of the league's harder shooters (91st percentile top shot speed by NHL Edge). His 2025-26 came with a warning from Evolving-Hockey: he was worth only 0.5 wins, dragged down by penalties and by what opponents created with him on the ice.

The recent stretch is the concern. He is pointless in four, and unlike the season as a whole, the chances have thinned out too, with his minutes down about a minute a night. With Artemi Panarin out, he's still on the top line with Alex Laferriere. Watch whether his shot volume comes back.
